title.zh: 电化学：原电池与电解池

description.zh: 两个电极“推电子”的本事不同（标准电极电势），接起来就有电压；放电时反应物减少、产物增多，按能斯特方程电压逐渐降低；充电就是用电把这个过程倒推回去，电解与法拉第定律管的正是这笔电与化学物质之间的账。理想标准状态模型，忽略过电势与内阻。
description.en: Two electrodes differ in how hard they push electrons (standard electrode potentials), so joining them gives a voltage. As discharge consumes reactants and builds up products, the Nernst equation says the voltage sags; charging pushes the whole process backwards, and electrolysis with Faraday's law keeps the ledger between charge and chemicals. An ideal standard-state model ignoring overpotential and internal resistance.

label.en: Two ways to get a voltage

reason.zh: 原电池靠化学反应给出电动势，感应靠磁通量变化给出电动势，两者都向外电路输出电压。
reason.en: A galvanic cell gets its emf from a chemical reaction and induction gets it from a changing flux; both drive a voltage into an external circuit.

reason.zh: E° 是单位电荷的能量差，与电场页的电势同一概念。
reason.en: E° is an energy difference per unit charge, the same idea as potential in the electric-fields lesson.

label.en: The logarithm in the Nernst equation

reason.zh: 反应商 Q 取对数后电压与 log Q 成直线，和玻尔兹曼因子是同一类指数关系。
reason.en: The voltage is linear in log Q, the same exponential relationship that appears in the Boltzmann factor.

title.zh: 电池为什么有电压，用着用着为什么变低？
title.en: Why does a battery have a voltage, and why does it sag with use?

ask.zh: 标准电极电势不同，两个电极接起来为什么会有电压？电压由什么决定？
ask.en: With different standard electrode potentials, why does joining two electrodes give a voltage? What sets its size?

ask.zh: 放电时反应物消耗、产物积累——能斯特方程说，浓度变化会让电压升高还是降低？
ask.en: As discharge consumes reactants and builds up products, does the Nernst equation say the voltage rises or falls?

ask.zh: 电解和电池放电是互逆过程——充电时外加电压要克服什么？和电磁感应里的能量转换有什么相通处？
ask.en: Electrolysis reverses battery discharge — what must the charging voltage overcome? What does that share with energy conversion in electromagnetic induction?

reveal.zh: 两电极电势差就是电压；用着用着反应物减少、产物增多，按能斯特方程电压逐渐降低。
reveal.en: The voltage is the difference of the two electrode potentials; as reactants are used up and products build, the Nernst equation drops the voltage.
